title: Psychosocial outcomes of risk-adapted prevention for familial and genetic prostate cancer predisposition (ProFam-Psych)
summary:
Prostate cancer is the most common cancer in men worldwide and the risk of developing the disease is significantly increased if there is a family or genetic predisposition. Men with an increased risk due to family/genetic predisposition suffer from daily worries and a higher level of prostate cancer-specific fear, overestimate their risk of developing the disease and show impairments in everyday life and increased depression values. Genetic testing is recommended for people with an increased risk of prostate cancer, but so far there are hardly any standardized preventive services and the psychosocial effects of genetic testing on those seeking advice are largely unknown.  A risk-adapted consultation center for people with an increased risk of prostate cancer (ProFam-Risk) is currently being implemented for the first time at the Düsseldorf University Hospital. During the consultation, men with an increased risk of prostate cancer are examined by a doctor, genetically tested and assigned to one of three risk categories (low, medium, high risk) based on their individual risk of developing the disease. They will also receive individual prevention recommendations. Men with a previously identified genetic mutation can also take part to receive individual advice and preventive recommendations. In addition, men with (previous) prostate cancer can also take part in the consultation in order to take advantage of genetic testing. The present study "Psychosocial outcomes of risk-adapted prevention for familial and genetic prostate cancer predisposition (ProFam-Psych)" aims to investigate the psychosocial effects of the risk-adapted ProFam-Risk consultation on those seeking advice. For this purpose, the psychosocial well-being of the participants in the consultation center is surveyed at 4 time-points using standardized questionnaires. Some of the participants will also be interviewed about their experiences. Inpatients with kidney or ureteral stones are collected as a comparison group.
This study is expected to provide information on the psychosocial effects of genetic testing and risk-adapted screening recommendations. In the future, the study will enable more well-founded cost-benefit considerations in genetic testing.

interventions.name: Persons with an increased risk of prostate cancer due to a familial/genetic predisposition who attend the risk-adapted prevention center "ProFam-Risk" are assessed at 4 time-points about various psychosocial factors (case group). 3 groups of people are included in the "ProFam-Risk" prevention consul
Persons undergoing inpatient treatment for an N20 diagnosis are assessed at two time points about various psychosocial factors (control group)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
case group
• Participation in the ProFam-Risk project
• Sufficient knowledge of German

control group
• Hospitalization for treatment Diagnosis of a kidney or ureter stone (N20)
• Sufficient knowledge of German
Exclusion criteria:
control group
• Prostate Cancer Disease
• Increased risk of prostate cancer: meet one of the following criteria:
         1. ≥ 2 second-degree relatives with diagnosed PCa
         2. a first-degree relative with PCa before the age of 60 
         3. Proven high-risk gene for PCa
